# Welcome {.unnumbered}

This is the reference site for **optimization-lab** — a from-scratch exploration of
applied mathematical optimization. The spark was working through Steven L. Brunton's
[*Optimization Bootcamp*](https://www.youtube.com/@eigensteve) [@brunton2026optimization],
but the site draws on the standard optimization literature broadly (see the
bibliography and the project's [`README`](https://github.com/ioannisantoniadis/optimization-lab)
for the full reading list) rather than following any one source chapter by chapter.

Three commitments shape everything here:

1. **Build it, don't just import it.** Every core algorithm is implemented from scratch
   in the `optimlab` Python package. Mature libraries are used deliberately as
   *correctness oracles* and *scale-up backends*, never as a substitute.
2. **Port a problem in, get solvers for free.** Every problem speaks one small `Problem`
   interface; every solver — from-scratch or backend — runs against any of them.
3. **See it, don't just prove it.** Every technique ships with an interactive visual —
   either right on the page (a live-rendered Plotly figure) or as a reactive
   [marimo](https://marimo.io) app you can drag sliders on.

## How this site is organized

Chapters are built up progressively, each landing once the corresponding `optimlab`
module is implemented and tested — see the project's
[`ROADMAP.md`](https://github.com/ioannisantoniadis/optimization-lab/blob/main/ROADMAP.md)
for the full phased plan. A chapter here is never
published ahead of the code it's explaining.

## Reading this site vs. reading the code

This site is the narrative — definitions, theorems, the "why" behind a design choice.
The `optimlab` package docstrings are the precise reference for a given function's
signature and behavior. When the two disagree, trust the code and open an issue: the
docstrings are regenerated from tests that actually run; this prose is written by hand
and can drift.
